messages:
AcmeSupport: hitting a weird failure when using tool calls through our Python + TS SDKs. The function gets selected fine, but args look munged on the server side, schema validation fails with 'unexpected type' for a bytes field. Repro steps and logs below.

Mira: sorry to hear that — can you paste the minimal repro and the exact SDK versions?

AcmeSupport: repro: python 3.11, redwood-sdk==1.8.2, ts client 2.0.1. Simple tool definition: 
```json
{"name":"upload_blob","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","contentEncoding":"base64"}}}}
```
Client call (py):
```py
client.call_tool("upload_blob", {"data": b"\x00\x01\x02"})
```
Server log: 
```
ValidationError: field 'data' expected base64 string, got 'AAEC\u0000' (string with embedded nulls)
Tool selector: selected upload_blob (v1)
Trace: toolcall.decode: malformed base64 padding at offset 3
```

AJ: hmm. That Python snippet is passing raw bytes — SDK should auto-b64 encode. Can you show exact wire payload from the SDK?

AcmeSupport: yes — attached captured payload (copied):
```
{"tool":"upload_blob","args":"AAEC\u0000"}
```

Devon: whoa the payload contains a literal u0000 escape sequence rather than proper base64. Looks like double-encoding or an inconsistent JSON encoder between layers. Which HTTP client are you using in Python? (requests/urllib3/httpx)

AcmeSupport: using requests via our internal wrapper. Tested with httpx same result. TS client sends: 
```ts
await client.callTool("upload_blob", { data: new Uint8Array([0,1,2]) })
```
Captured TS payload:
```
{"tool":"upload_blob","args":"AAEC\u0000"}
```

Mira: both SDKs producing same odd escape — maybe the SDK serializes a JS Buffer/py bytes into JSON with embedded null escapes, and the server expects strict base64. Can you try forcing explicit b64 in the arg to see if it changes behavior?

AcmeSupport: tried: python: base64.b64encode(b"\x00\x01\x02").decode() -> 'AAEC' -> payload becomes {"args":"AAEC"} (no \u0000). Server accepts that. So the SDK b64 path yields correct string but passing raw bytes yields the \u0000 escape.

SupportBot: (automated) Logged ticket #INC-2026, routing to eng-ml and sdk-teams.

AJ: possible root causes: 1) SDK tries to embed bytes directly into JSON string with C-style escapes, 2) our JSON encoder in the client layer uses ensure_ascii or similar causing null to be escaped as \u0000, 3) middleware double-encodes leading to truncated padding.

Devon: can you run a quick experiment: in Python, call json.dumps({"args": bytes_val}) with the same value and show output; and in TS run JSON.stringify({args: Buffer.from([0,1,2]).toString('binary')}) and also JSON.stringify({args: Buffer.from([0,1,2]).toString('base64')}). That will tell us whether the bytes are being coerced to a string before b64 path runs.

AcmeSupport: run results: python json.dumps coerces bytes to "b'\x00\x01\x02'" (so bytes->str representation). But our SDK wrapper intercepts and calls .decode('latin1') to keep bytes -> 1:1, then json.dumps turns embedded nulls into "\u0000" escapes. JS path: Buffer.toString('binary') produced '\u0000\u0001\u0002' when passed through JSON.stringify in our capture. So both languages get escaped nulls at JSON level.

Mira: ok that suggests the SDK's automatic branch that should detect raw bytes and base64 them isn't firing because bytes are being coerced into a string earlier in the wrapper. We'll need a patch: ensure byte-like types are detected before any decode/str coercion and call base64 encoder.

AJ: yes. For the short term, suggest customers pass base64 strings explicitly. For the SDK fix: 1) On Python, check for isinstance(arg, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)) before any decode hooks. 2) On TS, accept ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array/Buffer and call Buffer.from(...).toString('base64') when serializing args. Add unit tests for embedded nulls and for optional bytes fields when omitted vs null.

Devon: also add server-side tolerant validation: accept strings containing \u0000 escapes by trying to interpret them as latin1 binary -> base64 normalize, but only as fallback (and log). Don't silently accept; emit a warning event to the Console/Optimize so customers can see improper serialization.

AcmeSupport: appreciate the triage. ETA for patch? This is blocking a customer rollout.

Mira: patch branch created: sdk/bytes-serialize-fix, small PR incoming today. We'll also push a temporary support note documenting the explicit base64 workaround and link the incident.

SupportBot: (automated) PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/sdk/pulls/4321 by Mira. Linked INC-2026.

AJ: assigning to @Devon for server fallback change and to @Mira for SDK fix. Will follow up with a release plan (hotfix vs patch release).

AcmeSupport: thanks — will try explicit base64 today and report back. :thumbsup:

Mira: if you can share a minimal zip with your internal wrapper we can test integration quickly.

AcmeSupport: uploading now to the ticket.

Devon: noted. I'll add the fallback normalization with a DEBUG flag so we can roll it out behind a config for a fast mitigation.

AcmeSupport: confirmed explicit base64 workaround worked — thanks!

Mira: great. marking this thread as ongoing but have a clear mitigation and pending SDK/server fixes.

SupportBot: (automated) Incident INC-2026 status: investigating -> patching.
